taxonomy.subtopic: Vertical membrane-cytoskeleton linkage failure and increased osmotic fragility

questions.stem_html: A 14-year-old boy has intermittent jaundice and left upper-quadrant fullness. His father underwent splenectomy for a similar disorder. Hemoglobin is 10.4 g/dL, reticulocyte count is increased, mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration is elevated, and the direct antiglobulin test is negative. The accompanying schematic shows small red cells lacking central pallor and lysis beginning at a higher sodium chloride concentration than control cells. Which defect best explains these findings?

options.text_html: Impaired anchoring of the spectrin-based cytoskeleton to the erythrocyte lipid bilayer
Reduced synthesis of beta-globin chains within erythroid precursors
Failure of glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase to generate NADPH
Deficient pyruvate kinase activity with reduced erythrocyte ATP production
Loss of the glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchor for complement-regulatory proteins

questions.explanation_html: Hereditary spherocytosis is caused by defects in proteins such as ankyrin, spectrin, band 3, or protein 4.2 that maintain vertical attachment between the membrane skeleton and lipid bilayer. Progressive membrane loss lowers the surface-area-to-volume ratio, producing rigid spherocytes that are trapped and destroyed in the spleen. Because spherocytes cannot expand as well in hypotonic fluid, they lyse at higher sodium chloride concentrations than normal biconcave cells.

wrong_choice_explanations.2: Reduced beta-globin synthesis causes thalassemia with microcytosis and target cells rather than Coombs-negative spherocytes with increased osmotic fragility.
wrong_choice_explanations.3: G6PD deficiency causes oxidant-sensitive hemolysis with Heinz bodies and bite cells, not a chronic vertical membrane-linkage defect.
wrong_choice_explanations.4: Pyruvate kinase deficiency lowers ATP and can produce echinocytes; it does not characteristically increase mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration or form spherocytes.
wrong_choice_explanations.5: Loss of GPI-anchored CD55 and CD59 causes paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria with complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis.

questions.educational_objective: Defects in vertical erythrocyte membrane-cytoskeleton interactions cause membrane loss, spherocyte formation, splenic sequestration, and increased osmotic fragility.
